images.caption: Robert Stephenson & Hawthorn 550 v dc overhead Bo-Bo No.7284 of 1945, "Doug Tottman", one of four built for Kearsley Power Station, Lancashire 1928-45. First named "Kearsley No.4", it was the RSH continuation of a Hawthron Leslie design (see No.3682 "Kearsley Power Station No.1"). It was used there until 1982 when the CEGB rebuilt it as a battery loco and moved it to Heysham Nuclear Power Station where it was named "Heysham No.1". British Energy withdrew it in 2009. In preservation it was renamed "Doug Tottman". At the Electric Railway Museum, Coventry, 9/11.
images.alt: Robert Stephenson & Hawthorn 550 v dc overhead Bo-Bo No.7284 of 1945, "Doug Tottman", one of four built for Kearsley Power Station, Lancashire 1928-45. images.caption: English Electric Type 3B, 200 v dc overhead & battery, 35 hp 0-4-0 No.E905 of 1935, "Spondon No.1". The Type 3B was a standard EE type in the 1920's & 30's. It was built for the Derbyshire & Nottinghamshire Electric Power Company for use at their Spondon Power Staion, Derbs., one of 3 used there. It was withdrawn in 1984 - a long working life. At the Electric Railway Museum, Coventry, 9/11.
